title: Lessons from the States, Book II, Ode 4: The Zhâi Pin
note: Celebrating the diligence and reverence of the young wife of an officer, doing her part in sacrificial offerings.

verses.t:
She gathers the large duckweed,
By the banks of the stream in the southern valley.
She gathers the pondweed,
In those pools left by the floods.

She deposits what she gathers,
In her square baskets and round ones.
She boils it,
In her tripods and pans.

She sets forth her preparations,
Under the window in the ancestral chamber.
Who superintends the business?
It is (this) reverent young lady.
